main_text.head: LIBER SEPTIMVS. DE SICARIIS.
TITVLVS PRIMVS.
main_text.p: CVM homines ex natura ipsa arripuerint, hauserint, omnem honestam rationem esse expediendæ salutis, Leges vim aduersus illam illatam latæ de Sicariis vindicarunt: quarum primam hanc describimus.

Senatus Areopagiticus ius dicito de cæde, aut vulnere, non casu, sed voluntate, inflicto, de incendio item, & malo veneno hominis necandi causa dato.ΔΙΚΑΖΕΙΝ ΔΕ ΤΗΝ ΒΟΥΛΗΝ ΤΗΝ ΕΝ ΑΡΕΙΩ ΠΑΓΩ ΦΟΝΟΥ ΚΑΙ ΤΡΑΥΜΑΤΟΣ ΕΚ ΠΡΟΝΟΙΑΣ ΚΑΙ ΓΥΡΚΑΙΑΣ ΚΑΙ ΦΑΡΜΑΚΩΝ ΕΑΝ ΤΙΣ ΑΠΟΚΤΕΙΝΗ ΔΟΥΣ. [?]

Legem hanc descripsit Demosthenes ὡς τοῦ ἐξ Ἀρεοπαγιτικοῦ [?]. Quæstionem autem haberi vult ab Areopagitico Senatu, de quo in superioribus multa diximus, sed pauca dicenda adhuc superfunt, quæ huius sunt argumenti. Ternis diebus in mensis singulos iudicare solebant Areopagitæ, nempe, quinto, quarto, & tertio Kalendas cuiusque mensis, idque subdiali in loco. Pollux Lib. VIII. cap. X. καθ' ἕκαστον ὁ μὴν ἡμέραις ἐδίκαζον ἐφεξῆς, πέμπτῃ φθίνοντος, τετάρτῃ, τρίτῃ [?]. ἐν ὑπαίθρῳ ἐδίκαζοντο [?], atque id, vt sub dio iudicarent, non tantum in Areopagitico Senatu obseruatum est, sed etiam in omnibus de cædeiudiciis. Antipho [illegible, ~60 letters]. Noctu & in tenebris iudicabant, ne ad dicentes respicere possent, sed ad ea quæ dicebantur. Lucianus Hermotimo: [illegible, ~70 letters]. Quanti enim fuerit momenti reos vidisse, exemplo est Phryne, quæ, vt referunt Plutarchus in Hyperide, Athenæus Lib. XIII. & ex eo Eustathius, impietatis accusata, cum iam in eo esset, vt damnaretur, nudatis papillis, ob formæ decorem & eleganti am, secundis iudicum calculis absoluitur. Quæ vero obseruarentur in Areopagitarum iudiciis tria sunt præcipua, primum [illegible, ~20 letters], secundum

page.notes: Greek accents and breathings are not clearly legible at this resolution; the Greek is copied as far as the letters can be read, and uncertain words are marked [?]. The Antipho and Hermotimo Greek lines are too small to read letter by letter and are marked illegible. The italic marginal note's first word reads "ius" as printed, followed by "dicito"; the printed form may be a line-end abbreviation and should be checked against the original. The printed text ends mid-sentence at "secundum" and the catchword is the Greek word "λόγῳ" at the right foot. A faint digitiser credit at the lower right is left out.
